Research record / Preprint

Morphemes vs. Manifolds: Diagnosing Structural Blindness and Morphological Hijacking in Large Language Models via Finite Affine Orbits

Frozen-model audit and negative result record; interpret within the tested models and protocol.

v1.0.02026-08-25Zenodo
Evidence boundary

A Zenodo deposit is a citable public record; it does not by itself imply peer review, independent validation, or broader empirical generalization.

01 / record overview

What this record documents.

This preprint is the public record for the VARZIN study titled “Morphemes vs. Manifolds,” which audits whether structure recovered from finite-affine and constructed-language representations should be interpreted as semantic understanding. The current VARZIN reading treats detectable morphology, clustering, and geometric regularity as distinct from independent recovery of the intended semantic axes. The record is therefore presented as part of the project’s falsification-oriented evidence trail rather than as evidence of semantic emergence.

Research question

How much of the apparent structure recovered by language models reflects morphemic or representational regularity, and how much supports the stronger claim that intended semantic structure has been independently recovered?

This question is interpreted within the documented model, dataset, implementation, and evaluation procedure; it is not generalized beyond that evidence.

04 / contribution

What this record adds to the research trail.

The record anchors the negative-result side of the VARZIN language-model program: structural regularity can be detectable while stronger semantic interpretations remain unsupported under the tested procedures.

Version v1.0.0 is retained as a fixed, citable public deposit. Later VARZIN pages may refine interpretation, but they do not silently rewrite this versioned record.
